I traced the night-shift path from origin/main f2ccc138, using NIGHT_SHIFT.md, CLAUDE.md, CHECKPOINTS.md, the four skills, the 13 agent files, tools/README.md, checkpoint.mjs, gate.mjs, settings.json and the hook. I matched each command against the Claude Code permission docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions and /permission-modes, read today). My notes are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Shamble-Frontlines/dbb5e494-b49f-5970-85a2-528a1e15b24b/scratchpad/kit-v3-1/trace-night.md, which ends with DONE.

How the rules behave in auto mode (from the docs):
- Ask rules always force a prompt, even when a narrower allow rule also matches, and they apply to every part of a compound command (`&&`, `;`, `|`).
- A trailing ` *` also matches the bare command, so the paired bare rules (`git status` and `git status *`, for example) are redundant.
- Only timeout, time, nice, nohup, stdbuf, command, builtin, noglob and bare xargs are stripped before matching. xvfb-run and npx are not.
- Writes to protected paths (.git, and .claude apart from .claude/worktrees and agent-memory Markdown) go to the classifier even when an allow rule matches. Plain edits anywhere else in the working directory are auto-approved.
- Allow rules for Agent, wildcarded interpreters and package-manager run commands are dropped in auto mode.
- A second way to stall: if the classifier blocks 3 actions in a row, or 20 in a session, auto mode pauses and prompts. So a needed command left to the classifier is also a stall risk, not only one that hits an ask rule.

Main findings:
1. The prompt the stuck run waits on: PR Advisor run session_01FPXGo8GioEMFrCm8FhivMU has been waiting since 11:02:43Z on `cd <scratchpad>/pr26/tools && npm ci --silent 2>&1 | tail -3; ls node_modules | head; ls /opt/pw-browsers`. The `npm ci` part hit the ask rule `Bash(npm ci *)` (settings.json:119). The `ls /opt/pw-browsers` part is a read outside the working directories. (1) ORDER OF RULES
- Deny, then ask, then allow. "Rules are evaluated in order: deny, then ask, then allow. The first match in that order determines the outcome, and rule specificity doesn't change the order." (permissions)
- "An allow rule can't carve an exception out of a deny rule. The same precedence applies between ask and allow: a matching ask rule prompts even when a more specific allow rule also matches."
- A deny in any scope beats an allow in any other scope (settings page, "Settings precedence" and permissions "Settings precedence").
- Hooks: "PreToolUse hook decisions don't bypass permission rules ... a matching ask rule still prompts even when the hook returned allow." The exception is exit code 2: "A hook that exits with code 2 stops the tool call before permission rules are evaluated."

(2) BASH MATCHING
- Prefix form with a trailing space and star: `Bash(npm run *)`. A star anywhere is a wildcard. Put the star after the subcommand (`Bash(git log *)`, not `Bash(git * main)`).
- `Bash(npm ci *)` matches bare `npm ci` (single wildcard, space before it). Yes.
- Compound commands: recognized separators are &&, ||, ;, |, |&, &, and newlines. "A rule must match each subcommand independently." Deny and ask rules apply to any subcommand, including inside $(...), subshells and for-loops.
- An allow rule does not approve an unparseable tail such as `npm test &&`.
- cd: "A cd into a path inside your working directory or an additional directory is also read-only." A cd outside those directories is not in the read-only set and is checked on its own. cd followed by git prompts when the directory changes.
- Read-only set (ls, cat, head, tail, grep, find, wc, diff, stat, du, cd, read-only git) runs without a prompt in every mode, with listed exceptions (unquoted globs with write flags, unparseable commands, over 10,000 characters). In auto mode these can still wait for the classifier.
- Wrappers stripped before matching: timeout, time, nice, nohup, stdbuf, command, builtin, and bare xargs. npx, mise exec, devbox run and docker exec are not stripped.
- A Bash rule does not cover another form of the same program: `Bash(git push *)` does not stop `git -C . push`. Sandboxing is the OS-level stop.

(3) ASK RULES IN AUTO MODE AND UNWATCHED SESSIONS
- Auto mode: "Explicit ask rules still force a prompt." Content-scoped ask rules fall back to a prompt even when the classifier would allow the action.
- Headless claude -p (v2.1.302+, no permission mode set): "Calls needing approval are denied unless you approve them with an allow rule, hook, canUseTool callback, or --permission-prompt-tool." So in -p the ask rule DENIES, it does not wait. (permission-modes, "Tool calls denied in claude -p and Agent SDK runs"; headless)
- --permission-prompts none: "Anything that would prompt is denied unless a PermissionRequest hook allows it ... and the run continues." (headless)
- dontAsk: "the session never waits for input." In dontAsk, ask rules are denied, not prompted. (permission-modes)
- Cloud scheduled tasks (routines): WAIT. "A run still stops and waits for an answer in cases such as these: Actions that prompt even in auto mode: for example, an action that matches an ask rule" and "Repeated blocks ... a permission prompt appears in the run's session and waits until someone answers it." To answer, "open the run from the task's detail page." (routines, "Permission prompts during a run")
- Cloud sessions also wait on MCP connector approvals: "A session counts as inactive while it waits for you to approve an MCP connector tool call." (claude-code-on-the-web, "Environment expired")
- So the docs say -p denies and cloud scheduled tasks wait. The stuck run is consistent with the cloud behavior.

(4) AUTO-MODE CLASSIFIER
- Order: matching deny, ask and allow rules resolve first. "Actions matching your allow, ask, or deny rules resolve immediately, with these exceptions." Exceptions: content-matched ask rules still prompt; "Writes to protected paths route to the classifier even when an allow rule matches"; "No allow rule approves recognized rm and rmdir critical-path removals." So ALLOW RULES DO SKIP THE CLASSIFIER, except those exceptions.
- Everything else goes to the classifier. "If the classifier blocks, Claude receives the reason."
- Repeated blocks: "if the classifier blocks an action 3 times in a row or 20 times total, auto mode pauses and Claude Code resumes prompting." In a cloud run that is a wait.
- Broad allow rules are dropped on entering auto mode: blanket Bash(*) or PowerShell(*); wildcarded interpreters such as Bash(python*); package-manager run commands; Agent allow rules; Monitor allow rules. (5) RULE SYNTAX
- MCP: `mcp__<server>__<tool>`; `mcp__<server>__*` for all tools of one server; `mcp__<server>` also matches all tools of that server. Allow globs need a literal `mcp__<server>__` prefix; `mcp__*` as allow is skipped. Plugin servers: `mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__*`. Claude.ai connectors: `mcp__claude_ai_<server>__<tool>`. Parentheses on an mcp__ rule in a settings file cause the rule to be skipped. If the org sets a connector to ask, allow rules for it do not take effect.
- Read and Edit paths (gitignore syntax): `//path` = absolute from filesystem root; `~/path` = home; `/path` = relative to the settings file's directory (project settings: the working directory root, so `/CLAUDE.md` is not the filesystem root); `path` or `./path` = relative to cwd. For deny and ask rules, a relative pattern with one directory segment matches at any depth (`Read(secrets/**)`); for allow rules it is anchored (`Edit(src/**)` matches only cwd/src).
- A Read deny also blocks Edit and Write on that path. Edit rules also cover Bash redirections (>, >>), and tee. Read and Edit deny rules cover recognized file commands in Bash (cat, head, tail, sed, tee). They do NOT cover python or node scripts that open files themselves. Write, NotebookEdit and Glob path rules never match.
- WebFetch: `WebFetch(domain:example.com)` matches that host only; `WebFetch(domain:*.example.com)` matches subdomains; bare `WebFetch` in deny removes the tool from context.

(6) PRECEDENCE AND RELOAD
- Order: managed > command line (--settings) > project local > project shared (.claude/settings.json) > user. "no other level, including command line arguments, can override a managed permission rule." "if a tool is denied at any level, no other level can allow it."
- Lists merge across scopes (permissions.allow adds up); a project allow needs workspace trust. Interactive trust dialog covers this; -p and SDK sessions in a never-trusted folder do not use project allow rules (they print a warning). Deny and ask rules apply right away.
- Reload: "Claude Code watches your settings files and reloads them when they change, so it applies most edits to the running session without a restart, including edits to permissions, hooks ..." So a long-lived local session picks up edits to disk.
- Cloud sessions (settings page, "Settings in cloud sessions"): shared project settings are read when the session has one repository; "User and project local settings (~/.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json): not read." Managed: "Only server-managed settings reach the cloud session" (a managed-settings.json on a laptop does not).
- Routine clone timing (routines): "Each repository you add is cloned on every run." So a commit on main reaches the NEXT run, not one already running. "If a GitHub pull request event triggers the run and the pull request's repository is the task's first repository, that repository starts from the pull request's head commit instead." So the PR Advisor reads the PR's own .claude/settings.json, not main's. A PR that removes deny rules would change the reviewer's rules before its own review. This is an inference from two documented facts; the docs do not state it as a warning.
- Project defaultMode: the settings page says "auto and bypassPermissions don't take effect from project or local settings". dontAsk and acceptEdits are not excluded. Whether a project dontAsk overrides the routine's forced auto mode is NOT documented.

proposal.summary:
The proposal is written to /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Shamble-Frontlines/dbb5e494-b49f-5970-85a2-528a1e15b24b/scratchpad/kit-v3-1/proposal.md, with notes in proposer.md (ends with DONE) in the same folder. I based it on settings.json at f2ccc13 and re-checked it on main 4c24d07: #25 changed only docs since, so every line number still holds.

What happened: the PR #26 Advisor run (session_01FPXGo8GioEMFrCm8FhivMU) has waited since 11:02:43Z on one compound command. Its `npm ci` part hit the ask rule at line 119, and its `ls /opt/pw-browsers` part read outside the working folders. It had to install because neither the review worktree nor the run's own checkout had tools/node_modules.

Why one settings file can't do it alone: it serves three kinds of session with opposite rights. The night shift must never merge, the PR Advisor must merge but never commit, and day sessions edit .claude/ and merge on Mustafa's go. So the proposal has three layers:
1. Static allows for the forms routines really type: one exact npm ci from main's lockfile with --ignore-scripts, plus `npm rebuild gl`; the xvfb-run and --expose-gc forms; read-only git; git rm for .checkpoints; the gh api reads; and the GitHub MCP tools.
2. Static denies only for what CLAUDE.md forbids every session, or what nobody needs in phase 0: history rewrites, branch delete or move, git -* option bypasses, secret reads through Bash, gh api writes, gh pr merge and auto-merge, MCP file writes, npx, npm run/test and shell wrappers. Each deny was checked against every needed command.
3. A role guard: a PreToolUse hook keyed on SHAMBLE_ROLE, set in routine-only cloud environments. It enforces the routine-only nevers: night merges, edits to .claude/, CLAUDE.md, .github and the gate files, PR Advisor commits and pushes, unlisted WebFetch, installs. A PermissionRequest hook turns any leftover prompt into a denial.

All 16 ask rules go; the ask list ends empty. There are 13 procedure changes; the main ones: the PR Advisor first switches to origin/main, worktrees live in .gate/, installs come from main's lockfile and are linked into worktrees, Playwright runs without npx, no git -C, pushes always name the branch, and agents use memory: local.

Key risks still open: a PR-triggered run starts under the PR head's own .claude/ (a security finding), whether the mid-session settings swap works (untested), case sensitivity of rule patterns, every git fetch going to the classifier despite the allow rule, and gl's prebuilt-binary download. No routine has ever run a write step, so the write paths are a static audit, not observed behaviour.

I made no repository edit, commit, push, or routine or session change.

findings.rule: Authority / config source: the PR Advisor starts under the PR head's own .claude/, CLAUDE.md and .mcp.json (U-2, P-1)
findings.problem: The official routines doc says a PR-event run 'starts from the pull request's head commit'. The hooks doc says '-p or SDK session ... treats the folder as trusted, so hooks committed in a repository's .claude/settings.json run'. So the PR head decides the session's settings, SessionStart hooks (which can add context and an initial user message), disableAllHooks, .mcp.json servers, skills, agents and CLAUDE.md, which also feeds the classifier. All of this runs before P-1. P-1's diff check is carried out by a model whose instructions came from the PR. The repo is public with forking allowed (gh api, read-only). advisor.md:72 'skip forks' is only an instruction.
findings.attack: A PR whose .claude/settings.json drops the role guard and adds a SessionStart hook gets a session with merge rights that runs on the PR's terms.
findings.fix: Before kit-v3-1 ships: (1) set the PR Advisor trigger filter Author is one of [Mergincanli] and Is draft = false, so fork and outsider PRs never start a session (routines doc: PR filters). (2) Treat P-1 as a guard against honest mistakes only, not as a boundary, and write that down. (3) Ask Mustafa whether server-managed or managed settings are available on his plan. They are the only layer a repo can't override (permissions doc: managed settings, allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly, allowManagedHooksOnly). (4) Record the remaining risk in the threat model: a session already hijacked by injection opens a PR that changes the rules.

findings.rule: The Wasm/JS client is hostile: running PR or model-written code in a credentialed session
findings.problem: Permission rules and the PreToolUse guard see only the model's own tool calls. The permissions doc says Read and Edit denies 'don't apply to ... arbitrary subprocesses'. tools/preview.js:92 runs <dir>/shamble-core.js, shamble-game.js, --pre and eval snippets through vm.runInThisContext, which has full process and require access. P-6 feeds it .gate/pr<n>. P-6 also runs `cd .gate/pr<n> && node tools/gate.mjs`, which is the PR's own gate.mjs. Any such child process gets the session's GitHub access through the egress proxy (/root/.ccr/README.md) and can write .claude/settings*.json (for example disableAllHooks), the hook scripts, and main's node_modules through the proposed symlink. The ruleset (id 25069670) needs 0 approvals, and its required checks gate and smoke come from the PR's own workflow file (gate.yml runs on pull_request). Whether a merge goes through the proxy is UNVERIFIED (no write was tested).
findings.attack: Game code in a PR, or code the night shift wrote after reading a hostile page, runs under preview.js or the PR's gate.mjs and uses the session's GitHub identity, so no permission rule or hook sees it.
findings.fix: Never run PR-tree code in a session that holds merge rights. The PR Advisor should rely on the CI gate and smoke results, and send PRs that need sims or renders to needs-mustafa or a day session. Change gate.mjs to take a target tree, so main's gate checks the PR tree, and drop `cd .gate/pr<n> && node tools/gate.mjs` and the ln symlink. For the night shift, look into OS-level fencing (the Claude Code sandbox; bwrap and socat are not installed in this container, so it needs an environment setup script, untested). Add a ConfigChange hook that blocks project_settings and local_settings changes in routine roles (hooks doc: ConfigChange can block). Pin the guard script's sha256 in the hook command.

findings.rule: Deny rules are not a security boundary: git option forms get past both the new and the existing denies
findings.problem: The permissions doc says a deny 'isn't a security boundary around the program'. I tested git 2.43 on throwaway local repos in the scratchpad with no network. Git accepts unambiguous abbreviations of long options and bundled short options. The proposed denies match only the full spelling. Abbreviated forms of delete (on push and branch), amend, hard reset, upload-pack (on fetch and ls-remote) and open-files-in-pager (on grep) all worked, while the denies `*--delete*`, `* -d *`, `*--amend*`, `git reset --hard *`, `*--upload-pack*` and `*-O*` did not match them. Allowed rules skip the classifier ('resolve immediately', permission-modes doc), so `Bash(git grep *)`, `Bash(git ls-remote *)` and the existing `Bash(git fetch *)` each become a way to run a command with no review.
findings.attack: An abbreviated option on an allowed git subcommand deletes a cs/ branch, rewrites history or runs a command, with no prompt and no classifier.
findings.fix: Do not add `Bash(git grep *)` or `Bash(git ls-remote *)`. Use exact forms instead (for example `Bash(git ls-remote --heads origin cs/*)`, and replace git grep with the Grep tool). Narrow `Bash(git fetch *)` to `Bash(git fetch -q origin main)` and `Bash(git fetch origin)`. Move option checks into the role guard: parse argv and reject any option that is a prefix of a dangerous long option, or that bundles a dangerous short flag. Keep the GitHub ruleset as the backstop for main, and treat cs/ and claude/ branches as unprotected.

findings.problem: (a) By default a hook that can't start or exits with a code other than 0 or 2 is a non-blocking error, so the call goes ahead (hooks doc, 'Block the action when a hook fails'). The proposal's 'fail closed' covers only errors inside the script. (b) Handlers run in the current directory. A relative command such as `node .claude/hooks/routine-guard.mjs`, after a persisted `cd .gate/pr<n>`, resolves to the PR's copy or to nothing. (c) disableAllHooks in any non-managed settings file turns the guard off. (d) The PermissionRequest backstop denies without stopping, so a hijacked run keeps going past the classifier's 3-in-a-row brake.
findings.attack: Changing the working folder or the settings file quietly removes the guard, and every routine-only never is gone.
findings.fix: Write the hook command as `node "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.claude/hooks/routine-guard.mjs"` with `"onFailure": "block"` (v2.1.295+; routines ran 2.1.310). Make the backstop return behavior deny with interrupt: true and a report line. Add the ConfigChange block above. Fix the existing syntax-gate hook path the same way.

findings.rule: Information and authority channel: every session posts as Mergincanli
findings.problem: NIGHT_SHIFT.md:10-12 trusts only Mergincanli comments on #16, and :15-18 resumes any cs/ branch named in a Mergincanli status comment and runs its gate and its checkpoint's 'Next steps'. The proposal statically allows add_issue_comment, update_issue_comment and issue_write for every session, including the PR Advisor, which reads hostile PR text. GitHub can't tell a session from Mustafa (routines doc: actions 'appear as you').
findings.attack: An injected PR Advisor edits the queue or posts a status comment on #16, and the night shift treats it as Mustafa's work.
findings.fix: In the role guard: the PR Advisor may comment only on PRs (never on issue 16), may not use issue_write, and may edit only its own review comment. The night shift may comment only on #16 and on its own PRs. In NIGHT_SHIFT.md, a queue item or handoff runs only if it links to an advisor APPROVE naming a full SHA on a PR or plan the night shift can check. Write this channel into the threat model.

findings.problem: The only enforced merge check is 'a 40-hex expectedHeadSha'. Any session can read the current head, so this proves nothing about approval or about Mustafa's go. mcp__github__merge_pull_request is statically allowed in every session, and GitHub write tools not on the deny list are accepted by a cloud config rule, so new tools are allowed by default.
findings.attack: An injected session reads the head SHA and passes it, which satisfies the hook.
findings.fix: In the guard, refuse a merge when `git diff --name-only origin/main...<sha>` touches .claude/, CLAUDE.md, .github/ or the gate files (Mustafa merges those himself), when the head repo is not the base repo, or when the gate and smoke check-runs on that SHA are not success. Replace the GitHub MCP deny list with a per-role allowlist in the guard (deny any mcp__github__* tool not listed). Deny update_pull_request changes to base.

findings.rule: Supply chain: npm ci / npm rebuild gl / symlinked node_modules (U-11)
findings.problem: The exact npm ci string does not fix the working folder or the npm config. `npm rebuild gl` runs gl's install script without --ignore-scripts, so a project, tools or user .npmrc (for example node-options or a binary host), or a poisoned prebuild cache, changes what runs. prebuild-install's download is not covered by the lockfile hash (U-11). The shared symlink lets later code change main's installed tools.
findings.attack: A .npmrc in the tree or home folder, or a cached tarball, changes what the allowed rebuild runs or installs.
findings.fix: Install the toolkit in the environment's setup script from main's lockfile, into a folder outside the repo (verify how setup scripts run for PR runs). After the rebuild, check the sha256 of gl's .node binary against a hash committed on main, and if it doesn't match, run without gl. In the guard, refuse npm when any .npmrc exists in the tree or in home. Remove the ln allow.

findings.rule: Wildcard allows that skip the classifier
findings.problem: `Bash(node .gate/*)` also matches paths that climb out of .gate with `..`, and runs whatever file the model wrote, with no classifier. It is not in auto mode's dropped list, which names only blanket Bash, wildcarded interpreters, package-manager run commands, Agent and Monitor rules, so U-5 likely won't save it. `Bash(node tools/preview.js *)` with eval, evalshot and --pre is the same power. The earlier WRITE-GUARD intent (ask on preview.js eval, evalshot and --pre) was dropped without saying so. `ln -s ... .gate/*/tools/node_modules` and `git rm -r .checkpoints/*` take extra paths (U-12).
findings.attack: Injected text gets the model to write a script and run it through a rule the classifier never sees.
findings.fix: For routines, the guard allows preview.js eval only with tracked main tool snippets (tools/sim.js, reach.js, perfbots.js) and refuses --pre and evalshot. Drop `Bash(node .gate/*)` for routines and let the classifier review it. In the guard, refuse any path argument that contains `..` or leaves .gate/ or .checkpoints/.

findings.rule: Untrusted text on the WebFetch allowlist (N54)
findings.problem: settings.json:43-44,64-65 allow github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, docs.rs and crates.io. Anyone can publish there, and the night shift fetches with nobody watching.
findings.attack: A page on an allowed host carries instructions to an unattended run.
findings.fix: In the guard for routines, limit github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com to Mergincanli/Shamble-Frontlines plus a named list of upstream repos, and docs.rs and crates.io to named crates. Keep 'fetched text is data' in both prompts.

findings.problem: The denies cover `git config --list` and `-l` and `*extraheader*`, but other git config read forms, `cat .git/config`, ~/.gitconfig and /proc/self/environ stay readable. Public GitHub comments are a channel for anything read.
findings.attack: A config or environment read in another form, then posted in a public comment.
findings.fix: Add Read denies for .git/config, ~/.gitconfig and /proc/**. Allow `git config` only with exact read keys. Treat the GitHub write tools as the way data leaves the session and limit them per role (see above).

findings.problem: `gh pr ready *` takes any PR number and so can trigger the PR Advisor on any PR. The gh api write-flag denies miss stuck short forms (field flag joined to its value). `pkill -f checkpoint.mjs` matches any command line containing that text. `Read(//opt/pw-browsers/**)`, `node --version`, `sha256sum *`, the smoke.mjs forms and mkdir -p are fine.
findings.fix: Allow `gh pr ready` only for the session's own PR, checked in the guard. Move gh api write detection into the guard by parsing flags. Keep the rest.

findings.rule: Ask list empty, but prompts remain
findings.problem: The ask list does end empty, but routines can still hit prompts: protected-path writes go to the classifier, reads outside the working folders prompt, connector tools that the org set to ask always prompt, inbound cross-session messages are held for approval, and after repeated blocks the classifier pauses (permission-modes doc). Only the PermissionRequest backstop covers these, and it is untested in routines (U-6).
findings.attack: Not an attack: the stall comes back.
findings.fix: Do TEST-RUN (a) before the first night. Include one protected-path write, one connector call and one repeated-block case, and check that each ends in deny plus interrupt, not a wait.

attack.summary:
Verdict: FAIL. The proposal meets its stated goal: it removes all 16 ask rules, nothing obvious stalls, and many of its denies (gh pr merge, npx, git -*, history rewrites) are right. But it treats static rules and a repo-hosted hook as a security boundary, and against this threat model they are not one.

Three problems decide it, each with evidence:
1. **The PR Advisor starts under the PR's own rules.** The routines doc says a PR run starts from the PR head, and the hooks doc says committed hooks run in SDK sessions. So a PR's settings, hooks, CLAUDE.md and .mcp.json are in force before step P-1. The repo is public and forking is allowed.
2. **Anything the session runs as a program can do what the rules forbid.** preview.js runs the tree's game code with full Node access (preview.js:92), and P-6 runs the PR's own gate.mjs. Such programs have the session's GitHub access through the proxy and can rewrite .claude/. The ruleset on main needs 0 approvals, and its required checks come from the PR's own workflow file.
3. **The git denies match only one spelling.** On throwaway local repos (git 2.43), abbreviated long options deleted a branch, amended a commit, hard-reset, and ran a command through fetch, ls-remote and grep, all past the denies. Since allowed commands skip the classifier, `git grep *`, `git ls-remote *` and the existing `git fetch *` become ways to run commands with no review.

The role guard can also fail open: a relative hook path, no `onFailure: "block"`, `disableAllHooks`, and a backstop that denies but doesn't stop the run. Two smaller gaps: every session posts as Mergincanli, so a hijacked PR Advisor can write to the night queue; and the merge check accepts any 40-character SHA.

**Must change before it ships:**
- **Trigger:** filter the PR Advisor routine to Author = Mergincanli and not draft.
- **No PR code with merge rights:** the PR Advisor runs no PR-tree code. It uses the CI gate and smoke results, and main's gate is changed to take a target tree.
- **Guard hardening:** an absolute hook path with `onFailure: "block"`, a ConfigChange hook that blocks settings changes in routines, and the guard script's hash pinned in the hook command.
- **Exact rules:** exact forms instead of the git grep and ls-remote wildcards, a narrower git fetch, and option parsing in the guard.
- **Per-role GitHub limits:** an allowlist of GitHub tools per role, the PR Advisor kept off issue #16, and the merge check also refusing PRs that touch the rules, PRs from forks, and heads whose checks aren't green.
- **Installs:** toolkit installed in the environment setup script, with the gl binary checked against a pinned sha256.
- **Fetch limits:** github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com limited to named repos for routines.
- **Test first:** TEST-RUN (a) before any night, including the prompt cases the backstop must turn into deny plus stop.

**Not verified:** whether a merge through the proxy works (I made no write), whether routines fire on fork PRs, whether the sandbox works in cloud containers (bwrap and socat are absent here), and how setup scripts behave for PR runs.
